mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES stays near -80% while TRANSIT remains similarly depressed, commuter-linked retail demand will keep falling over the next four weeks because fewer trips generate fewer discretionary retail visits.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remaining at or below their current depressed levels.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in GROCERY_PHARM after an extreme trough should slightly lift retail-and-recreation within one to two weeks because routine essential trips spill into nearby nonessential shopping when households resume stocking behavior.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises at least 5 points from its weekly low
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within 14 days after GROCERY_PHARM recovers from its recent trough by at least 5 points.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS stays deeply negative while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, consumers are substituting home-based activity for out-of-home leisure, so RETAIL_REC will remain below its recent average over the next month.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains below -70 while RESIDENTIAL stays above +30
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days even though PARKS stays below -70 and RESIDENTIAL stays above +30 for most of that period.

mechanism_narrative: A short-lag retail recovery should start only after TRANSIT stops falling and holds above the prior week's level, because easier movement to commercial areas restores shopping trips within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises week-on-week after being below -85
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve in the week after TRANSIT turns upward from below -85.

mechanism_narrative: If residential staying-home pressure remains high while workplaces remain heavily suppressed, the next four weeks should bring lower retail mobility because households keep consolidating errands and avoiding discretionary trips.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated and WORKPLACES stays near its current depressed level.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent improvement in GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT indicates more necessary movement and broader travel access, which should raise RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks through trip chaining and incidental shopping.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT both rise week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve within 14 days after both GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT rise together.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES remains near its current trough and TRANSIT does not recover, retail demand will stay weak for four weeks because formal activity and commuting remain suppressed, limiting exposure to stores.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES stays below -75 and TRANSIT stays below -80
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises meaningfully over the next 28 days while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain below the stated thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained reduction in PARKS mobility relative to the prior week signals adverse outdoor conditions or a weak leisure season, and that should translate into lower retail-and-recreation spending within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls another 5 points from the current weekly mean
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in the week after PARKS falls by at least 5 points from its current weekly mean.
